problem: The note says "|x(t)|² is instantaneous power" without the 1 Ω condition, while the 1 Ω condition is applied only to the units of E. A reader can carry away the idea that |x|² is power in general, which is false when x is a voltage or current.
fix: Write: "|x(t)|² is the instantaneous power only when the signal is a voltage across a 1 Ω resistor (or a current through 1 Ω); otherwise treat it as the squared magnitude of x."

where: Section 1, DT energy and power formula note
problem: "P the same units per sample" is dimensionally wrong. The count 2N+1 is a pure number, so dividing by it does not change units; DT average power has the same units as DT energy, namely (sample value)².
fix: "E and P both have units of (sample value)²; the divisor 2N+1 is a pure sample count and adds no unit."

problem: The rational-ratio rule for sums of periodic signals is a CT result. It is placed right after the DT sentence, so a student may conclude that a sum of DT periodic signals can be aperiodic. In DT the periods are integers, so a common multiple always exists and the sum is always periodic.
fix: Add: "This rational-ratio test matters in CT. In DT every period is an integer, so integer periods always have a common multiple and a sum of DT periodic signals is always periodic; its fundamental period is the LCM of the individual sample periods."
